unit.title: Launch: Proficiency Goals & the Seal of Biliteracy

lesson.title: Speed Self-Check: Numbers, Questions, Courtesy & Survival Phrases
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Set a timer if you want the full effect. Today is a fast-paced self-check across four practical categories — numbers, question words, courtesy phrases, and survival phrases. None of this assumes you've taken Spanish before; treat it as your second data point for this week's baseline, right alongside yesterday's can-do statements.

Four categories, one purpose — see what's already familiar and what isn't, honestly and quickly:

NUMBERS: cero, uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez... up through veinte (twenty) for now.
QUESTION WORDS: qué (what), quién (who), cómo (how), dónde (where), cuándo (when), por qué (why), cuánto (how much/many).
COURTESY PHRASES: por favor (please), gracias (thank you), de nada (you're welcome), perdón / disculpe (excuse me / pardon).
SURVIVAL PHRASES: No entiendo (I don't understand), ¿Puede repetir, por favor? (Can you repeat, please?), ¿Dónde está...? (Where is...?), Necesito ayuda (I need help).

This is exactly the kind of practical, everyday language this course builds toward all year — you're not expected to have it locked in yet, in week one. Move through the self-check below quickly, trust your first instinct, and don't stop to worry over the ones you miss.

Numbers, questions, courtesy, and survival phrases: four practical categories down, and a second honest data point for your baseline. Tomorrow you put everything from this week together into one written commitment: your own proficiency goal statement.

objectives: Recall basic Spanish numbers, question words, courtesy phrases, and survival phrases at a rapid pace
Use the self-check results as a second data point for this week's proficiency baseline
materialsNeeded: Optional: a timer, for the intended fast pace
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Set the fast-paced framing explicitly — this is a speed self-check, not a test to study for.
2. Read through all four categories together once at a normal pace.
3. Time the student (optional) doing a quick self-quiz out loud on a few items from each category before the digital activity.
4. Complete the cloze self-check activity.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's goal-statement writing task.
differentiationTips: Struggling: if most categories feel brand-new, that's an entirely normal week-one result — note it honestly as the baseline and move on without dwelling
Ready for more: have them add three more items to any one category from memory or a quick search, and quiz a family member with their additions

This lesson uses a written self-check instead of audio (the scope-and-sequence's original 'speed-review carousel' framing) because no TTS/audio-generation infrastructure exists yet in the platform (open decision, expansion-plan-2026-09.md §12.9) — the written self-check tests the same recall speed the audio version would.

rows.problem: Write the Spanish word for 'thank you' and for 'you're welcome.'
